meta.title: Nejimakidori model catalog
meta.scope: Current working source; not a production checkpoint inventory
meta.description: Public tensors, shared representations, predictions and training flow.

features.name: candidate_hand_counts
features.title: Candidate hand counts
features.description: Integer occupancy tensor over deduplicated candidate hands and 34 ordinary tile types; red fives contribute to their ordinary type counts.
features.encoding: First axis: hand-bank slot, with slot 0 the current hand. Validity is determined by candidate_hand_valid.

features.name: candidate_hand_red
features.title: Candidate hand red
features.description: Per-candidate red-five occupancy by suit, represented separately from ordinary type counts.
features.encoding: First axis: hand-bank slot, with slot 0 the current hand. Validity is determined by candidate_hand_valid.

features.name: candidate_melds
features.title: Candidate melds
features.description: Per-candidate public meld histogram indexed by lowest tile type and six meld/red channels.
features.encoding: Axes: hand slot, lowest meld tile (34), channel (6). Channels: 0 chi, 1 pon, 2 open kan, 3 closed kan, 4 added kan, 5 red-five counts at their ordinary five tile.

features.name: candidate_hand_valid
features.title: Candidate hand valid
features.description: Binary occupancy mask for the 96-entry candidate-hand axis.
features.encoding: First axis: hand-bank slot, with slot 0 the current hand. Validity is determined by candidate_hand_valid.

features.name: discard_candidate_hand
features.title: Discard candidate hand
features.description: Gather indices from 37 discard actions into the deduplicated candidate-hand bank. Routing only; excluded from the learned board projection.
features.encoding: Integer index into the 96-slot hand bank. Action legality masks determine which entries are meaningful.

features.name: chi_candidate_hand
features.title: Chi candidate hand
features.description: Gather indices from the chi-pattern × follow-up-discard action grid into the candidate-hand bank. Routing only; excluded from the learned board projection.
features.encoding: Integer index into the 96-slot hand bank. Action legality masks determine which entries are meaningful.

features.name: pon_candidate_hand
features.title: Pon candidate hand
features.description: Gather indices from the pon × follow-up-discard action grid into the candidate-hand bank. Routing only; excluded from the learned board projection.
features.encoding: Integer index into the 96-slot hand bank. Action legality masks determine which entries are meaningful.

features.name: kan_candidate_hand
features.title: Kan candidate hand
features.description: Gather indices from tile-specific kan candidates into the candidate-hand bank. Routing only; excluded from the learned board projection.
features.encoding: Integer index into the 96-slot hand bank. Action legality masks determine which entries are meaningful.

features.name: river_pre_tile_id
features.title: River pre tile id
features.description: Pre-riichi opponent-sequence channel: ordinary tile-type IDs.
features.encoding: Axes: opponent (seats 1–3), right-aligned recent discard slot (32). Validity is determined by the corresponding sequence mask.

features.name: river_pre_is_red
features.title: River pre is red
features.description: Pre-riichi opponent-sequence channel: binary red-five attributes.
features.encoding: Axes: opponent (seats 1–3), right-aligned recent discard slot (32). Validity is determined by the corresponding sequence mask.

features.name: river_pre_tsumogiri

features.encoding: Axes: opponent (seats 1–3), right-aligned recent discard slot (32). Validity is determined by the corresponding sequence mask.

features.name: river_pre_tedashi_relation
features.title: River pre tedashi relation
features.description: Pre-riichi opponent-sequence channel: categorical same/nearby-tile relation to the previous comparable hand discard.
features.encoding: Axes: opponent (seats 1–3), right-aligned recent discard slot (32). Validity is determined by the corresponding sequence mask.

features.name: river_pre_tedashi_gap

features.name: meld_type
features.title: Meld type
features.description: Categorical observed-meld kind with zero padding, indexed by relative player and meld slot.
features.encoding: 0 padding, 1 chi, 2 pon, 3 open kan, 4 closed kan, 5 added kan. Valid slots are marked by meld_valid.

features.name: meld_tile_ids
features.title: Meld tile ids
features.description: Ordinary tile-type IDs for public meld constituent slots.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: meld_tile_red
features.title: Meld tile red
features.description: Binary red-five indicators aligned with public meld constituent slots.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: meld_tile_valid
features.title: Meld tile valid
features.description: Binary occupancy mask over public meld constituent slots.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: meld_source
features.title: Meld source
features.description: Categorical actor-relative source-seat index for each public call, with zero for closed/no-source entries.
features.encoding: 0 closed/no source; otherwise actor-relative source seat + 1.

features.name: meld_call_age
features.title: Meld call age
features.description: Clipped event-distance scalar from the original meld event, normalized by 100.
features.encoding: min(1, elapsed public events / 100); axes: four relative players × four meld slots.

features.name: meld_upgrade_age
features.title: Meld upgrade age
features.description: Clipped event-distance scalar from an added-kan upgrade, normalized by 100.
features.encoding: min(1, elapsed public events / 100); axes: four relative players × four meld slots.

features.name: meld_valid
features.title: Meld valid
features.description: Binary occupancy mask over each player’s four public meld slots.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: current_draw_tile_id
features.title: Current draw tile id
features.description: Ordinary tile-type ID of the current self draw, interpreted under current_draw_valid.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: current_draw_is_red
features.title: Current draw is red
features.description: Binary red-five indicator for the current self draw.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: current_draw_valid
features.title: Current draw valid
features.description: Binary validity mask for current-draw identity channels.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: normal_self_shanten
features.title: Normal self shanten
features.description: Clipped categorical standard-hand shanten encoding; category equals actual shanten + 1 until saturation.
features.encoding: 0 complete, 1 tenpai, 2 one-shanten, 3 two-shanten, 4 three-or-more shanten; 5 marks an unavailable special family with fixed melds.

features.name: chiitoitsu_self_shanten
features.title: Chiitoitsu self shanten
features.description: Clipped categorical seven-pairs shanten encoding with a distinct infeasible-family sentinel when fixed melds exist.
features.encoding: 0 complete, 1 tenpai, 2 one-shanten, 3 two-shanten, 4 three-or-more shanten; 5 marks an unavailable special family with fixed melds.

features.name: kokushi_self_shanten
features.title: Kokushi self shanten
features.description: Clipped categorical thirteen-orphans shanten encoding with a distinct infeasible-family sentinel when fixed melds exist.
features.encoding: 0 complete, 1 tenpai, 2 one-shanten, 3 two-shanten, 4 three-or-more shanten; 5 marks an unavailable special family with fixed melds.

features.name: closed_hand
features.title: Closed hand
features.description: Binary closed-hand predicate used by structural/scoring constraints.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: self_efficiency
features.title: Self efficiency
features.description: Three normalized self-hand statistics: actual shanten, improving-type cardinality and available improving-copy count.
features.encoding: Last axis: [actual shanten / 8, improving tile types / 34, available improving copies / 80].

features.name: self_yaku_possibility
features.title: Self yaku possibility
features.description: Nineteen binary public structural-feasibility channels for the current self hand.
features.encoding: Last axis (boolean public feasibility, not win probability): 0 tanyao, 1 haku, 2 hatsu, 3 chun, 4 round wind, 5 seat wind, 6 honitsu, 7 chinitsu, 8 toitoi, 9 chiitoitsu, 10 shousangen, 11 daisangen, 12 tsuuiisou, 13 chinroutou, 14 honroutou, 15 kokushi, 16 chanta, 17 junchan, 18 iipeikou.

features.name: dora_multiplicity
features.title: Dora multiplicity
features.description: Per-ordinary-tile integer multiplicity induced by visible dora indicators.
features.encoding: 34 ordinary tile types; each count records how many visible indicators award dora to that tile type.

features.name: public_visible_red_counts
features.title: Public visible red counts
features.description: Public red-five occupancy by suit, excluding concealed self occupancy.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: known_unavailable_counts
features.title: Known unavailable counts
features.description: Per-ordinary-tile unavailable-copy count combining public exposures and the self hand.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: prevailing_wind
features.title: Prevailing wind
features.description: Categorical current-round wind ID.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: kyoku_number
features.title: Kyoku number
features.description: Zero-based current-hand index within the native round: s.kyoku − 1.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: dealer_relative_seat
features.title: Dealer relative seat
features.description: Categorical dealer index in actor-relative seat coordinates.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: honba
features.title: Honba
features.description: Integer repeat-counter scalar conditioning settlement transfers.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: riichi_sticks
features.title: Riichi sticks
features.description: Integer count of accepted riichi deposits in the current table pot.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: live_wall_count
features.title: Live wall count
features.description: Integer remaining ordinary-draw count; excludes replacement draws.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: total_kan_count
features.title: Total kan count
features.description: Integer kan count in the current hand.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: nominal_all_last
features.title: Nominal all last
features.description: Binary nominal-final-hand predicate.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: dealer_currently_leads
features.title: Dealer currently leads
features.description: Binary predicate that the dealer has rank 1 under current score ordering.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: any_player_at_or_above_30000
features.title: Any player at or above 30000
features.description: Binary score-threshold predicate used by match termination conditions.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: scheduled_hands_remaining
features.title: Scheduled hands remaining
features.description: Nonnegative scheduled-hand count for the fixed continuation model.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: seat_context
features.title: Seat context
features.description: Two normalized per-player coordinates: score/100000 and rank/4.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: score_extrema
features.title: Score extrema
features.description: Minimum and maximum player scores, normalized by 100000.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: seat_wind
features.title: Seat wind
features.description: Categorical player-wind IDs in actor-relative player order.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: open_opponent_yaku_possibility
features.title: Open opponent yaku possibility
features.description: Thirteen-channel public feasibility subset, populated for opponents with observed open calls.
features.encoding: Last axis (boolean public feasibility, not win probability): 0 tanyao, 1 haku, 2 hatsu, 3 chun, 4 round wind, 5 seat wind, 6 honitsu, 7 chinitsu, 8 toitoi, 9 shousangen, 10 honroutou, 11 chanta, 12 junchan.

features.name: opponent_called_tile_count
features.title: Opponent called tile count
features.description: Observed open-meld tile cardinality per opponent; self slot remains zero.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: opponent_discard_count
features.title: Opponent discard count
features.description: Integer public discard-sequence length per relative player.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: last_tedashi_tile
features.title: Last tedashi tile
features.description: 37-class one-hot encoding of each player’s most recent non-tsumogiri discard.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: riichi_push_count
features.title: Riichi push count
features.description: Player×riichi-target count of non-tsumogiri discards lacking established safe-tile evidence.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: genbutsu_to_seat
features.title: Genbutsu to seat
features.description: Binary player×tile public safe-tile relation derived from observed discard and riichi history.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: passed_unchanged_to_seat
features.title: Passed unchanged to seat
features.description: Binary player×tile passed-discard relation retained across intervals without relevant hand changes.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: blocker_counts
features.title: Blocker counts
features.description: Tile×remaining-copy histogram over native outside-relation blocker types.
features.encoding: Axes: tile type, remaining-copy count 0–4 of adjacent outside-relation blocker tiles.

features.name: sotogawa_earliest_turn_to_seat
features.title: Sotogawa earliest turn to seat
features.description: Earliest qualifying opening-discard index for each player×outside-tile relation; zero encodes absence.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: win_kind
features.title: Win kind
features.description: Categorical optional-win context: none, ron or tsumo.
features.encoding: 0 outside a win decision, 1 ron, 2 tsumo.

features.name: decision_phase
features.title: Decision phase
features.description: Categorical phase selecting the native action contract; numeric phase IDs differ from TRAIN_POLICY_HEADS indices.
features.encoding: 0 DISCARD, 1 RESPONSE, 2 KAN, 3 RIICHI, 4 WIN.

features.name: trigger_tile_id
features.title: Trigger tile id
features.description: Ordinary tile-type ID of the event-conditioned trigger.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: trigger_is_red
features.title: Trigger is red
features.description: Binary red-five attribute of the trigger tile.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: trigger_valid
features.title: Trigger valid
features.description: Binary validity mask for trigger identity channels.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: trigger_source
features.title: Trigger source
features.description: Actor-relative source-seat ID of the triggering event.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: riichi_state
features.title: Riichi state
features.description: Per-player categorical state encoded as declared + accepted flags.
features.encoding: Actor-relative seats; declared flag + accepted flag: 0 none, 1 declared, 2 accepted.

features.name: ippatsu_alive
features.title: Ippatsu alive
features.description: Binary per-player ippatsu eligibility under observed intervening events.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: rinshan_state

features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: riichi_legal_mask

features.name: chi_discard_legal

features.description: CHI binary support over pattern×follow-up-discard actions.

features.name: chi_discard_shanten
features.title: Chi discard shanten
features.description: CHI pattern×follow-up-discard shanten categories, actual shanten + 1.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: chi_discard_ukeire_count
features.title: Chi discard ukeire count
features.description: CHI pattern×follow-up-discard available improving-copy counts.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: pon_discard_legal
features.title: Pon discard legal
features.description: PON binary support over pattern×follow-up-discard actions.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: pon_discard_shanten
features.title: Pon discard shanten
features.description: PON pattern×follow-up-discard shanten categories, actual shanten + 1.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: pon_discard_ukeire_count
features.title: Pon discard ukeire count
features.description: PON pattern×follow-up-discard available improving-copy counts.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: kan_legal_mask
features.title: Kan legal mask
features.description: Binary support mask over decline and 34 tile-specific kan actions.
features.encoding: Shapes exclude batch; seats are actor-relative (self 0, opponents 1–3). Masks use 0/1.

features.name: chi_call_efficiency
features.title: Chi call efficiency
features.description: CHI normalized shanten/improving-type/improving-copy statistics after the call.

nodes.title: Public state tensors
nodes.summary: Actor-relative native feature tensors and deterministic post-action hand indices.
details: Inference inputs exclude opponent concealed-hand state and supervised hidden-state labels.
The native schema fixes tensor order, scalar dtype, shape and byte offset.

nodes.title: Shared hand bank
nodes.summary: Shared suit-local residual convolutions produce embeddings for occupied candidate-hand entries.
details: Each suit stack uses kernel-3 convolutions with dilation rates 1, 2 and 4 and residual LayerNorm/GELU updates.
Honor-tile features use a separate 128-dimensional GELU projection.
Ordinary/red tile occupancy and six-channel meld features are conditioned on a projected public-state vector.

Occupied hand entries use 16-row buckets up to 128 rows and 512-row buckets above that; deduplicated suit rows use 16 or 4096. Padding is removed before scattering 512-wide encodings into the hand bank.

nodes.title: Shared river encoder
nodes.summary: A parameter-tied convolutional encoder processes pre-riichi and post-riichi opponent discard sequences.
details: Validity masking is reapplied after each convolution; padded tokens and empty streams remain zero.
Flattened ordered stream embeddings and max-pooled summaries enter the board projection.
Mean- and max-pooled stream embeddings also enter per-player critic descriptors.
The computation graph contains neither river self-attention nor candidate-to-river cross-attention.

nodes.title: Residual board trunk
nodes.summary: Concatenated public scalars, hand-bank summaries and river embeddings enter a four-block residual MLP.
details: Numeric channels are cast to float32, flattened and transformed by elementwise arcsinh.
Yaku-feasibility axes use shared linear basis projections grouped by channel width.
Each pre-normalized residual block expands 512→1536 with GELU, contracts to 512 and adds the skip connection.
The terminal board representation is normalized in float32 with center=False, scale=False and epsilon=1e−5.

nodes.title: Decision candidates
nodes.summary: Action-indexed embeddings combine hand-bank gathers, shared board context and deterministic action descriptors.
details: The canonical index space partitions into 37 discard, 74 riichi/discard, 149 response and 35 kan slots.
The 150-way response head appends an open-kan score gathered from the triggering tile’s kan candidate.
Only active candidate rows enter learned evaluation; absent candidate slots are constant padding.
WIN maps both policy branches to current-hand candidate 260; there is no separate accept/decline value estimator.

nodes.title: Opponent beliefs
nodes.summary: Categorical shanten/count marginals and conditional Bernoulli improving-tile marginals share the board encoder.
details: Observed meld counts define support lower bounds; unavailable-copy counts define support upper bounds.
Count projection enforces concealed-hand cardinality and tile-copy availability constraints.
Riichi or four fixed melds mask non-tenpai shanten logits.
Outputs are constrained marginals; they do not parameterize a normalized joint distribution over concealed hands.

nodes.title: Tile interaction refinement
nodes.summary: Two opponent-shared transformer blocks apply additive residual corrections to count and conditional-ukeire logits.
details: Pre-LayerNorm self-attention and 64→128→64 GELU residual MLPs share parameters across opponents.
Token inputs concatenate initial marginal probabilities, tile identity, availability, meld lower bounds, shanten probabilities and projected board context.
A zero-initialized 64→14 projection produces ordinary/red count and four shanten-conditioned ukeire corrections.
The shanten logits are not modified by this residual attention output.

nodes.title: Policy and completion heads
nodes.summary: A shared scalar candidate-scoring head is partitioned and gathered into phase-specific policy logits.
details: Candidate features include three route-affinity logits and three opponent-ron logits.
Board-conditioned heads produce binary win/pass logits and per-player ron/tsumo completion-yaku and score-state logits.
Native legality masks, opening-symmetry pooling and final-wall safety transforms precede action selection.
MMD optimizes legal-action probability mass against detached Q and reference-policy KL terms; supervised restoration is a separate objective.

nodes.title: Four-player context
nodes.summary: A shared affine/GELU map embeds four distinct player descriptors conditioned on a common candidate representation.
details: The self indicator and dealer indicator are independent descriptor coordinates; they can both equal one for the acting player.
Descriptors concatenate observed meld identities, seat-wind scoring consequences, dora, score/rank context and public opponent evidence.
Action-conditioned coordinates encode projected ordinary draws, chi-turn eligibility and discard-source identity.
Parameter sharing does not imply identical player embeddings or permutation invariance of the full seat-ordered encoder.

nodes.title: Joint hand critic
nodes.summary: Shared player/role projections parameterize event, conditional-deposit and claim-score factors of a current-hand outcome model.
details: Nonlinear role pooling produces logits over whole winner/draw masks; player win probabilities are not independently factorized.
Claim heads parameterize added-bonus-han categories and conditional hand-score support.
Hand-score factors for simultaneous winning claimants retain the conditional product factorization.
Call-conditioned predictions model attempted calls, including priority preemption by competing claims.

nodes.title: Rule-based settlement
nodes.summary: A deterministic support decoder maps event, claim-score and deposit states to transfers, scores and ranks.
details: Triple-ron support is mapped to the simulator’s abort event.
Public yaku, fu, bonus and settlement-legality masks restrict probability support.
Unsupported liability/nagashi allocations are masked from payment NLL and retained in support-coverage statistics.

nodes.title: Fixed match continuation
nodes.summary: A fixed score-to-rank continuation model supplies per-settlement payoffs for critic expectations.
details: Terminal settlements use realized score/rank state, deterministic tie priority and rounded ST3.
Nonterminal forecasts condition on post-hand scores, scheduled hands remaining and future dealer counts.
The common Gumbel scale is the square root of a positive quadratic variance; a positive dealer-count coefficient shifts score locations.
The graph contains no learned state-value head or final-match-return regression target.

blocks.title: Win/pass head

operations.title: Dense 2

operations.title: Legality mask
operations.description: Apply native win/pass support. Both branches use the same current-hand Q in MMD.

blocks.title: Deterministic player descriptors

operations.title: Public descriptor assembly

operations.title: Action role append

operations.title: Common context concatenation

operations.title: Dense + GELU
operations.description: Project all common channels, excluding the trailing 4 ×465 player descriptors.

blocks.title: Shared player projection
blocks.summary: Apply the same affine/GELU map to each descriptor concatenated with common context.
blocks.sharing: All four seats share one Dense 64; queued future splits are not implemented

operations.title: Dense 64 + GELU
operations.description: One parameter set for self and all three opponents. Self/dealer are independent input coordinates, not separate network branches.
operations.sharing: Shared across all four seats and action candidates

blocks.title: Joint-event role network
blocks.summary: Nonlinear role pooling scores each of 49 whole terminal events.

operations.title: Common event Dense
operations.description: Project common context into 16 event channels.

operations.title: Event-kind embedding
operations.description: Four terminal-event kinds receive learned 16-channel embeddings.

operations.title: Three player-role Dense maps
operations.description: Separate winner/source/ready projections are shared over players, then pooled according to each whole-event role mask.
operations.sharing: Distinct by role; tied across seats and 49 events

operations.title: Sum + GELU
operations.description: Combine common, kind and pooled player-role terms before event scoring.
operations.sharing: One functional form for all events

operations.title: Dense scalar
operations.description: Shared linear score produces one logit per whole event.

blocks.title: Claim-state projection
blocks.summary: Embed recipient, ron payer and win-kind coordinates for 16 unique winning claims.
blocks.sharing: One claim encoder; tsumo payer shares are not separately learned

operations.title: Recipient/payer gather
operations.description: Gather recipient 64, payer 64 for ron only (zero for tsumo), and two-way win-kind one-hot.

operations.title: Dense + GELU
operations.description: Shared claim-state transform. Tsumo payer shares later reuse the same winner state.
operations.sharing: Shared across 12 ron and 4 tsumo winners

blocks.title: Added-bonus-han head
blocks.summary: Linear categorical added-han readout with public open/riichi constraints.
blocks.sharing: One bonus readout across claim roles

operations.title: Dense 14
operations.description: Score the 14 added-bonus-han categories for each unique winning claim.

operations.title: Public support mask
operations.description: Exclude added-han categories incompatible with open-hand and required-riichi status.

blocks.title: Conditional hand-score head
blocks.summary: Predict categorical score support conditioned on claim state and added bonus han.
blocks.sharing: Shared conditional hand-score network

operations.title: Bonus embedding + GELU
operations.description: Add one of 14 learned 64-channel bonus embeddings to the claim state before GELU.

operations.title: Dense 38
operations.description: Append scaled known meld fu to the 64-channel conditional state and score 38 han/fu states.
operations.sharing: One score head across claims and bonus conditions

operations.title: Share gather + legal-score mask
operations.description: Reuse each tsumo winner score for its three payer shares and apply public score constraints.
operations.sharing: Identical tsumo score distribution across its payer shares

blocks.title: Conditional deposit-mask network
blocks.summary: Score 16 whole deposit masks conditioned on each joint event.
blocks.sharing: Shared conditional-mask scorer; joint masks remain whole outcomes

operations.title: Event-context Dense
operations.description: Project 16 event channels into 8 deposit-context channels.

operations.title: Player Dense and mask pooling
operations.description: Project each player 64→8 and sum selected players for each deposit mask.
operations.sharing: Shared over all seats and masks

operations.title: Role-count Dense
operations.description: Project three event-role counts induced by each deposit mask.

operations.title: Sum + GELU + Dense scalar
operations.description: Combine the three 8-wide terms, apply GELU and score each conditional mask.

blocks.title: Deterministic settlement decoder
blocks.summary: Apply event/deposit and score support, normalize factors and derive legal payment distributions.
blocks.sharing: No learned settlement-rule branch

operations.title: Event/deposit support
operations.description: Joint event/deposit legality and normalization restrict the learned factor logits.

operations.title: Transfer and marginal decoding
operations.description: Combine conditioned claim-score support and joint masks into payment marginals.

blocks.title: Fixed continuation and expected value
blocks.summary: Map settlement score states to fixed rank forecasts and compute expected normalized objective.
blocks.sharing: Fixed continuation mapping for all candidates

operations.title: Fixed Gumbel continuation
operations.description: Use score locations, future dealer counts and a time-dependent common scale to estimate final placement probabilities.
operations.sharing: Fixed fitted parameters; not trained by current MMD

operations.title: Objective expectation
operations.description: Convert each settlement payoff to J=ST3/100+P(first)−P(fourth), then integrate under the critic distribution.

objective.description: Sum supported payment NLL and valid-row critic constraints, including directional terms. The critic AdamW update uses synchronized dense gradients with per-variable clipping.

objective.title: MMD actor pass objective
objective.description: Negative detached-Q policy gain plus 0.3 KL(current∥previous), 0.3 KL(current∥production) and 0.01 actor constraints. Logged entropy has zero objective coefficient.

notes: Detached Q is a coefficient in ∇θρ: the expected-value gradient is −Σc stop_gradient(Qc)∇θρc.
Critic-private parameters receive no actor update. Shared representation updates can alter subsequent critic predictions despite the detached evaluation path.
The previous-policy expected-Q contribution is constant with respect to current parameters. Both KL terms differentiate only the current distribution.
WIN maps current and previous policies to the same Dirac mass at candidate 260; the Q-gain gradient vanishes for that phase, while head-level KL gradients remain.
constraint_divergence detaches its constrained target logits; it does not globally detach constrained predictions consumed by downstream actor operations.
The fixed continuation constants and production SavedModel parameters are excluded from both improvement optimizers.
Mirror and production policies consume the same public inputs. Their input edges are omitted; their detached output dependencies are explicit.

symbols.name: normalize_draw_payments
symbols.description:
Remove native draw deltas' already-paid riichi deposits.

Nagashi and zero-transfer exhaustive draws can retain the per-seat
deposit delta. MJAI reach_accepted already accounts for that payment.
Accept only the observed, conservation-checked native defect.

symbols.name: CompletionScoreCoupling
symbols.description:
Lift score tails to the lower bounds implied by the same completion.

Compatible yaku marginals are never added as if independent. Exclusive
alternatives can be summed; the strongest exclusive-set bound wins.

outputs.name: discard_policy_logits
outputs.title: Discard policy logits
outputs.description: Legality-constrained categorical action logits over 34 ordinary tile classes plus three red-five classes.

outputs.name: riichi_policy_logits
outputs.title: Riichi policy logits
outputs.description: Joint categorical action logits over declaration status × discard class: 37 dama choices followed by 37 riichi choices.

outputs.name: response_policy_logits
outputs.title: Response policy logits
outputs.description: Categorical action logits with support [pass, 3×37 chi/discard, 1×37 pon/discard, open kan]; total width 150.

outputs.name: kan_action_logits
outputs.title: Kan action logits
outputs.description: Categorical logits over decline followed by 34 tile-indexed kan candidates; total width 35.

outputs.name: win_decision_logits
outputs.title: Win decision logits
outputs.description: Two categorical logits: decline (0), accept the currently legal ron/tsumo opportunity (1). Apply softmax on the last axis.

outputs.name: opponent_shanten_logits
outputs.title: Opponent shanten logits
outputs.description: Categorical logits over four clipped shanten classes per opponent; class 0 denotes tenpai. Public constraints mask non-tenpai support where required.

outputs.name: riichi_action_logits
outputs.title: Riichi action logits
outputs.description: Branch log-masses obtained by logsumexp over discard classes for dama and riichi; softmax yields the declaration marginal.

outputs.name: response_action_logits
outputs.title: Response action logits
outputs.description: Branch log-masses for pass, chi, pon and open kan, computed by logsumexp over compatible joint response actions.

outputs.name: chi_pattern_logits
outputs.title: Chi pattern logits
outputs.description: Logsumexp aggregates over follow-up discards for each of the three chi patterns; softmax gives the pattern distribution conditional on the chi branch.

outputs.name: terminal_payment_probabilities
outputs.title: Terminal payment probabilities
outputs.description: Policy-mixture categorical transfer marginals indexed by payment kind, payer, recipient and amount-support class.

outputs.name: payment_values
outputs.title: Payment values
outputs.description: Per-position monetary support vector: fixed PAYMENT_VALUES followed by four public-state-dependent bank atoms.

outputs.name: final_placement_probabilities
outputs.title: Final placement probabilities
outputs.description: Policy-mixture actor final-rank marginal obtained by integrating current-hand outcomes through the fixed continuation distribution.

outputs.name: review_outcome_probabilities
outputs.title: Review outcome probabilities
outputs.description: Policy-mixture marginal over seven disjoint event categories: deal-in, actor win, tenpai draw, noten draw, opponent tsumo, other ron and abort.

outputs.name: settlement_mean
outputs.title: Settlement mean
outputs.description: First moment of policy-mixture honba-free net transfers for actor-relative players 0–3 and bank. The underlying joint support retains inter-transfer covariance.

outputs.name: settlement_variance
outputs.title: Settlement variance
outputs.description: Elementwise second central moment of policy-mixture honba-free player/bank net transfers: max(E[X²] − E[X]², 0).

outputs.name: critic_expected_points
outputs.title: Critic expected points
outputs.description: Per-active-candidate expected post-hand score minus current score for four actor-relative players, in points.

outputs.name: critic_action_indices
outputs.title: Critic action indices
outputs.description: Sparse row index pairs [input-position index, canonical critic-action index]. All other critic_* outputs share this row ordering.

auxiliaries.name: route_affinity_logits
auxiliaries.title: Route affinity
auxiliaries.description: Three candidate-conditioned Bernoulli logits for visible shortest-route support: tanyao, flush and outside-hand. Sigmoid outputs are concatenated into downstream actor/critic context.

auxiliaries.name: candidate_ron_logits
auxiliaries.title: Candidate ron risk
auxiliaries.description: Three candidate-conditioned opponent ron-risk logits concatenated into the actor’s final candidate representation. This branch is absent from CriticTrainer’s feature path.

auxiliaries.name: constraint_loss
auxiliaries.title: Actor structural constraints
auxiliaries.description: Per-position sum of belief, route and completion-yaku/score projection divergences. The MMD actor objective applies coefficient 0.01.

auxiliaries.name: opponent_ukeire_by_shanten_logits
auxiliaries.title: Opponent ukeire by shanten logits
auxiliaries.description: Internal network output; not exported for serving. Independent Bernoulli logits over 34 structural improving-tile indicators, conditional on each opponent’s shanten class; apply sigmoid.

auxiliaries.name: opponent_ukeire_logits
auxiliaries.title: Opponent ukeire logits
auxiliaries.description: Internal network output; not exported for serving. Bernoulli log-odds after marginalizing conditional improving-tile probabilities over the categorical shanten distribution.

auxiliaries.name: opponent_wait_logits
auxiliaries.title: Opponent wait logits
auxiliaries.description: Internal network output; not exported for serving. Bernoulli log-odds for joint tenpai-and-structural-wait events. The probability is P(shanten=0)·P(tile improves | shanten=0); furiten and yaku legality are not equivalent to this event.

auxiliaries.name: opponent_hand_count_logits
auxiliaries.title: Opponent hand count logits
auxiliaries.description: Internal network output; not exported for serving. Categorical logits over counts 0–4 for each ordinary/red tile class and opponent, after support masking and count projection. Counts include observed meld occupancy.

auxiliaries.name: round_completion_yaku_logits
auxiliaries.title: Round completion yaku logits
auxiliaries.description: Internal network output; not exported for serving. Constrained Bernoulli logits for 23 yaku labels on the highest-scoring completion of the next observed tenpai shape, indexed by player and ron/tsumo. This conditional completion target is not a win-probability target.

auxiliaries.name: round_completion_score_logits
auxiliaries.title: Round completion score logits
auxiliaries.description: Internal network output; not exported for serving. Constrained categorical logits over SCORE_STATES for the corresponding next-tenpai completion, indexed by player and ron/tsumo; apply softmax on the last axis.

training.title: Mortal match
training.description: Collect 10,000 standard-South trajectories against the fixed Mortal opponent using 2,500 wall seeds and all four learner-seat rotations. Convert recoverable decisions from every seat into observed current-hand transfer supervision.

training.title: Observed settlement fit
training.description: Perform one finite pass of supported played-action transfer-vector NLL plus critic constraints. Gradients propagate through critic-private parameters and connected shared representation paths; unplayed candidates have no supervised transfer target.

training.title: Magnetic mirror descent
training.description: Perform one finite MMD pass over retained decisions, using detached critic expectations, a phase-frozen previous-policy reference and a run-frozen production reference. Actor constraint coefficient: 0.01.

training.title: Balanced root reruns
training.description: Sample equal counts of eligible targeted roots and unfiltered normal roots, with two continuations per root. Eligibility strata are Q disagreement, tenpai, keiten, improving calls, riichi, public threat and sakigiri. Q disagreement threshold: 0.0025 J.

training.title: Train roots and descendants
training.description: Apply the same critic→actor pass sequence to all retained root and continuation rows. Forced root actions and opponent actions supply off-policy experience, not cross-entropy policy targets.
training.formula: all retained root and descendant rows → critic → actor

training.title: Optimization and replicas
training.description: Use independent AdamW optimizer states for actor and critic: learning rate 5e−6, weight decay 1e−4 and per-variable clipnorm 1. Sum dense gradients across replicas once before clipping. Exclude padding from masked reductions; physical batch layout can still affect floating-point updates.

training.title: Independent next match
training.description: Evaluate each updated checkpoint on the next disjoint 10,000-game seed block. Reuse that match as the next iteration’s data; terminate after the final evaluation without a subsequent optimizer pass.

training.title: Separate structural restoration
training.description: Separate supervised restoration losses consume observed action labels and hidden-state targets. These losses are not included in the current MMD improvement schedule.

mathematics.title: Legal policy normalization
mathematics.description: Select the native active head, right-pad to width 150, apply the exact legality mask and compute float32 log_softmax. Masked logits use the finite −10⁹ sentinel; their exponentials underflow to zero under the normal float32 logit scale. Native head indices and decision_phase IDs are distinct enumerations.

mathematics.title: Observed payment likelihood
mathematics.description: Maximize the likelihood of the observed transfer vector conditional on the recorded action by marginalizing compatible latent event, deposit and score states. The objective is not an independent-cell composite likelihood. Ambiguous zero-transfer observations remain marginalized; simultaneous-claim score factors preserve the implemented conditional product factorization.

mathematics.title: From hand outcomes to action value
mathematics.description: Integrate action-conditioned scored-event/deposit probabilities against public-state settlement utilities. Compute the deterministic continuation payoff tensor once per position and reuse it across candidate rows. Observed transfer supervision applies only to recorded/rerun actions; Q for unplayed candidates is model-based.

mathematics.title: Fixed Gumbel continuation
mathematics.description: Independent common-scale Gumbel perturbations of nonterminal score locations induce a Plackett–Luce permutation distribution. Locations and scale use 10,000-point units. Softplus-transformed coefficients are fixed constants. Terminal states bypass the continuation distribution and use deterministic rank, first-place pot assignment and ceiling-rounded ST3.

mathematics.title: Magnetic mirror descent objective
mathematics.description: For each match/root phase, refresh the previous-policy snapshot before one critic pass followed by one actor pass. Hold production parameters fixed across the run. Critic-private variables; no actor update reaches them through Q.
Stop-gradient: retain the forward value and set its derivative to zero.
Belief, route-affinity and completion-yaku/score structural constraints.
Valid-row mask. Reductions normalize across replicas; padding exclusion is not numerical batching invariance.

mathematics.title: Detached constraint targets
mathematics.description: Minimize KL from a stop-gradient constrained distribution to the raw predictive distribution. This target detach is local to the constraint objective and does not detach constrained predictions on ordinary downstream paths. Directional critic regularization additionally detaches the entire input state before finite odds perturbations.

mathematics.title: Shared parameters, four distinct player representations
mathematics.description: Apply the same affine/GELU projection to four player-specific descriptors concatenated with common candidate context. Self and dealer are independent descriptor predicates, concatenated with public-state features and river aggregates. Dealer status also conditions deterministic settlement support. Parameter tying does not impose representation equality or global permutation invariance.

Event-role indicators for winner, source and exhaustive-draw readiness.
Embedding of the event kind.
One shared scalar event-scoring vector, applied to each event representation.

mathematics.title: Tile-attention refinement
mathematics.description: Apply two pre-LayerNorm residual self-attention/MLP blocks to each opponent’s 34×64 token matrix. Four heads use key dimension 16 and scaled-dot-product denominator 4. Parameters are tied across opponent axes. A zero-initialized 64→14 output projection produces additive ordinary-count, red-count and conditional-ukeire logit residuals.

64×14 residual-output matrix, applied to each row token; initialized to zero.

vocabulary.description: Four-player axes are actor-relative: self 0, next player 1, opposite 2, previous 3. Three-opponent axes omit self.

"""Prepare source archives and build the joint training dataset."""

import argparse
import fcntl
import json
import os
import pathlib
import types

from log_dataset import download, player_ranks


def run(args):
    root = pathlib.Path(args.output).resolve()
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with (root / "pipeline.lock").open("a") as lock:
        fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        plan = vars(args).copy()
        del plan["workers"]
        for name in ("archives", "databases", "output", "reserve"):
            if plan[name] is not None:
                plan[name] = str(pathlib.Path(plan[name]).resolve())
        plan["extra_archives"] = [
            str(pathlib.Path(path).resolve()) for path in args.extra_archives
        ]
        if (root / "pipeline.json").exists():
            previous = json.loads((root / "pipeline.json").read_text())
            previous.pop("workers", None)
            if previous != plan:
                raise ValueError("Dataset inputs changed; use a fresh output")
        else:
            temporary = root / "pipeline.json.partial"
            temporary.write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=2) + "\n")
            temporary.replace(root / "pipeline.json")
        archives = args.archives
        if archives is None:
            archives = root / "downloads"
            download.run(archives)
        if args.databases:
            enriched = root / "archives"
            if not (enriched / "player_ranks.json").exists():
                player_ranks.run(archives, args.databases, enriched)
            archives = enriched
        # Record building is CPU work, including its spawned workers.
        os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = "-1"
        from log_dataset import training_data

        training_data.run(
            types.SimpleNamespace(
                archives=str(archives),
                extra_archives=args.extra_archives,
                output=str(root / "data"),
                reserve=args.reserve,
                workers=args.workers,
                limit_games=args.limit_games,
            )
        )


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--archives",
        help="Existing archives; omit to download pinned Houou logs",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--databases",
        help="Historical rank databases; omit for enriched archives",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--extra-archives", action="append", default=[])
    parser.add_argument("--reserve", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=24)
    parser.add_argument("--limit-games", type=int)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.archives is None and args.databases is None:
        parser.error(
            "downloading archives requires --databases for rank enrichment"
        )
    if args.workers < 1 or (
        args.limit_games is not None and args.limit_games < 1
    ):
        parser.error("workers and limit-games must be positive")
    run(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Build the Linux native collector for the current Python interpreter."""

import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys


def run():
    root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    target = pathlib.Path(
        os.environ.get(
            "CARGO_TARGET_DIR", root / "log_dataset/native_collection/target"
        )
    ).resolve()
    subprocess.run(
        [
            "cargo",
            "build",
            "--locked",
            "--release",
            "--manifest-path",
            str(root / "log_dataset/native_collection/Cargo.toml"),
        ],
        cwd=root,
        env={
            **os.environ,
            "PYO3_PYTHON": sys.executable,
            "CARGO_TARGET_DIR": str(target),
        },
        check=True,
    )
    destination = root / "log_dataset/_native_collection.so"
    temporary = destination.with_suffix(".so.tmp")
    shutil.copyfile(target / "release/lib_native_collection.so", temporary)
    temporary.replace(destination)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

"""Download and verify the fixed Houou MJAI corpus."""

import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import shutil
import urllib.request
import zipfile

HOUOU_MJAI_RELEASE = "https://github.com/NikkeTryHard/tenhou-to-mjai/"
HOUOU_MJAI_ARCHIVES = {
    2024: (
        HOUOU_MJAI_RELEASE + "releases/download/v2.0.0/2024.zip",
        "4c0bb20ebdc263ab5819d848b620f6bf36304ccb70914722fd89b524be3afa1f",
    ),
    2025: (
        HOUOU_MJAI_RELEASE + "releases/download/v2.0.0/2025.zip",
        "0274e3f2a3b4ed32cd9af6d0f9895c061c5141e63bb6c90e561f349043b7a771",
    ),
}


def file_checksum(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as input_file:
        return hashlib.file_digest(input_file, "sha256").hexdigest()


def validate_archive(path, expected_checksum):
    summary_path = path.parent / "player_ranks.json"
    if summary_path.exists():
        summary = json.loads(summary_path.read_text())["years"][path.stem]
        if summary["archive_sha256"] != expected_checksum:
            raise ValueError(f"source SHA256 mismatch: {path}")
        expected_checksum = summary["merged_sha256"]
    if file_checksum(path) != expected_checksum:
        raise ValueError(f"SHA256 mismatch: {path}")
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:
        names = archive.namelist()
        if not names or any(not name.endswith(".mjson") for name in names):
            raise ValueError(f"Expected a nonempty MJAI archive: {path}")


def fetch_archive(output, year):
    path = output / f"{year}.zip"
    part_path = output / f".{year}.zip.part"
    url, expected_checksum = HOUOU_MJAI_ARCHIVES[year]
    if path.exists():
        validate_archive(path, expected_checksum)
        return path
    if part_path.exists() and file_checksum(part_path) == expected_checksum:
        validate_archive(part_path, expected_checksum)
        part_path.replace(path)
        return path
    offset = part_path.stat().st_size if part_path.exists() else 0
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        url,
        headers={
            "User-Agent": "nejimakidori-model/1",
            **({"Range": f"bytes={offset}-"} if offset else {}),
        },
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
        append = offset > 0 and response.status == 206
        if response.status == 206 and not response.headers[
            "Content-Range"
        ].startswith(f"bytes {offset}-"):
            raise ValueError(f"Incorrect download resume offset: {url}")
        with part_path.open("ab" if append else "wb") as output_file:
            shutil.copyfileobj(response, output_file, length=1024 * 1024)
    validate_archive(part_path, expected_checksum)
    part_path.replace(path)
    return path


def run(output):
    """Return verified archive paths, resuming interrupted downloads."""
    output = pathlib.Path(output).resolve()
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if (output / "player_ranks.json").exists():
        paths = [output / f"{year}.zip" for year in HOUOU_MJAI_ARCHIVES]
        for path in paths:
            validate_archive(path, HOUOU_MJAI_ARCHIVES[int(path.stem)][1])
        return paths
    return [fetch_archive(output, year) for year in HOUOU_MJAI_ARCHIVES]

# Native features and self-play

Rust handles RiichiEnv replay, legal transitions, scoring and the Python
interface. C++ calculates board and candidate-hand features. Both recorded
positions and self-play use this engine.

## Build

Complete the [repository setup](../../README.md#setup), including the patched
RiichiEnv checkout, then run from the repository root:

```sh
python -m log_dataset.build_native_collection
```

This builds `log_dataset/_native_collection.so`. The build needs Rust, a C++17
compiler and `ar`. Rebuild after changing native code or the input layout.

## Input tensors

[src/schema.rs](src/schema.rs) defines field names, shapes, dtypes and packed
order. The build derives C++ offsets from those declarations. Inspect the
installed library's schema with:

```sh
python -c 'from log_dataset import _native_collection as n; print(n.INPUTS)'
```

Shapes exclude the batch dimension. Seats are actor-relative unless the producer
explicitly converts them. Packed rows contain consecutive fields in declaration
order, without alignment padding. `training.self_play.FEATURE_DTYPE` exposes NumPy
views of those rows.

The contract contains 125 tensors, 34,966 scalar elements and 43,358 bytes per
packed row. The eight `discard_action_{normal,all}_upgrade_` fields
(`valid`, `type_count`, `tile_count`, `weighted_gain`) are removed. They were
unpopulated and excluded from learning by zero substitution. Extraction now
omits them, and the encoder has no retired-input substitution path. Nyanten's
explicit upgrade-analysis API is independent of the model input contract.

The four `*_candidate_hand` tensors are gather indices, not learned numeric
features. They remain in the transport contract. Dora indicator IDs and their
validity mask are removed; `dora_multiplicity` remains for learned features and
deterministic scoring. Removing those ten scalar inputs also changes the hand
bank's board-conditioning projection. The main board projection is now
`[9055, 512]`: 296 formerly zero upgrade rows and 229 index/dora rows have been
removed from its original input layout.

Previous checkpoints cannot be loaded strictly into this model. The index/dora
pruning removes learned contributions, so weight transfer alone does not imply
output parity. The separate removal of the learned `sakigiri_order` branch also changes actor
weights; see [model compatibility](../../model/ARCHITECTURE.md#from-a-game-state-to-an-action).
Reference policies require an explicit compatible export and validation before
training; the current source exposes the 125-input signature.
Existing exports keep their original signatures; the training runtime does not
adapt between contracts. Rebuild datasets from source under the current schema.

Self-shanten fields encode actual shanten + 1: 0 is complete, 1 is tenpai,
and 2 is one away. Target samplers must account for that offset.

### Action-conditioned win values

`action_win_value_range` has axes `[295, closed/open, ron/tsumo, min/max]`;
`action_win_value_valid` marks legal, available completions. Closed dama actions
are scored without riichi. Declaration actions and actions after accepted
riichi include it. No-yaku dama has zero ron range and a false ron-valid flag;
its menzen-tsumo completion can still be legal. One-shanten searches preserve
the action's declaration state rather than assuming a later riichi.

These fields replace `action_value_range` and `action_value_valid`, which assumed
riichi for every closed hand. Rebuild recorded datasets from source archives and
collect fresh replay before training with this contract. Old TFRecords are
rejected because the new required fields are absent; renaming old fields does
not repair their values. Old exports retain their original input contract and
must not be paired with this encoder. Warm-start weights require retraining
and evaluation with the corrected features before publication.

The retired fixed-reference scoring tensors are absent. The selected fixed
reference policy does not consume them, and they never entered learned encoder
projections. Declared-riichi candidate ranges are computed explicitly for legal
riichi actions; other candidate evaluations no longer calculate an unused
forced-riichi scoring bank. Removing these tensors changes the input signature
and packed layout but no learned tensor shape.

Collector requests contain public feature rows, legal actions and trajectory
indices. MMD supervises observed payments reconstructed from completed logs;
the native collector does not calculate unused hidden-hand or counterfactual
ron labels. Expert restoration labels are generated by recorded replay.

The former prior-only scoring fields and `policy_prior_values` binding are
removed. Their dama/extra-han and hypothetical closed-hand scoring branches had
no model consumer. Legal action completion ranges retain their scoring contract.

| Source | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| [src/features.rs](src/features.rs) | Public-state snapshots and legal post-call hands. |
| [cpp/features.cpp](cpp/features.cpp) | Table, river and meld features. |
| [cpp/candidate.cpp](cpp/candidate.cpp) | Candidate hands, action masks and efficiency features. |
| [cpp/yaku.cpp](cpp/yaku.cpp) | Public yaku feasibility and fixed-meld values. |
| [cpp/scoring.cpp](cpp/scoring.cpp) | Completion search, with scoring delegated to RiichiEnv. |
| [src/lib.rs](src/lib.rs) | Python bindings. |

Opponent concealed hands are excluded from feature snapshots. Feature packing
returns only the model input contract. Historical dataset focus metadata and
its native sampling analysis are removed.

## Collector interface

`NativeCollector` runs complete games through three operations:

1. `next()` returns pending decisions and packed feature rows, or `None` when
   finished.
2. `submit(codes)` supplies one legal action per pending decision.
3. `finish()` returns completed game logs and counters.

[training/self_play.py](../../training/self_play.py) batches worker
requests for inference and retains their packed rows for training. Completed
worker results contain actions, behavior probabilities and targets.

`snapshot(decision)` captures a pending decision between `next()` and
`submit()`, including every simultaneous request in that game. The returned
root exposes `decision` (its local request offset) and
`fork(copies, seed, shuffle_remaining=True, *, until_hand_end=False)`.
With `until_hand_end=True`, each branch stops after its current hand settles.
The log retains the following hand's start as a completion boundary, or the
real `end_game` when the match ends. Collection reconstructs payments only
for completed hands; the pending following hand contributes no training rows.
Forks retain public history, concealed hands, pending actions and prefix logs. They shuffle unrevealed wall
tiles without moving revealed dora indicators, and seed future hands from the
branch seed. Duplicate-wall forks apply the same physical-tile permutation to
each player's remaining queue, preserving queue order, counterclockwise
borrowing and the shared rinshan tiles. With shuffling disabled, the initial
engine state is identical; subsequent collector randomness still uses the supplied seed. Repeated forks
with the same seed are reproducible. The parent collector is unchanged.
These continuations condition on the captured hidden hands rather than drawing
an information-set posterior. Python collection emits only suffix decisions.
Hand counters count completed hands, including the initial partial hand of a
fork. Riichi turn totals include declarations before the root in that hand,
matching the retained riichi flags and completed-hand denominators. Fork
statistics describe root-conditioned continuations, not ordinary match rates.

`NativeCollector.from_match(events_json, seed, duplicate)` recreates a seeded
evaluation trajectory. Call `next()` to inspect its pending decisions and
`submit_recorded()` to advance the recorded actions. Replay verifies every
generated event against the supplied log, including discard origin, consumed
tiles and settlements; incompatible seeds or simulator histories fail.
Triple-ron abortive draws (`sanchaho`) reconstruct all three legal ron claims:
the log records one draw event rather than three individual wins. Unobserved
losing claims are replayed as passes only to reconstruct the public trajectory;
they are not action labels. Snapshots fork out of replay mode,
and simultaneous claims in counterfactual branches follow the supplied policy.

Action heads and dimensions are defined in
[model/actions.py](../../model/actions.py). SavedModel exports expose their
input and output schemas through the `serving_default` signature.

```sh
python -m pytest integration/big/test_native_collection.py \
  integration/big/test_feature_generation.py \

```

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum Dtype {
    INT8,
    INT16,
    FLOAT16,
    FLOAT32,
}
impl Dtype {
    pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::INT8 => "int8",
            Self::INT16 => "int16",
            Self::FLOAT16 => "float16",
            Self::FLOAT32 => "float32",
        }
    }
    const fn width(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::INT8 => 1,
            Self::INT16 | Self::FLOAT16 => 2,
            Self::FLOAT32 => 4,
        }
    }
}
pub struct Field {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub shape: &'static [usize],
    pub dtype: Dtype,
    pub count: usize,
    pub width: usize,
    pub offset: usize,
    pub size: usize,
}
const fn layout<const N: usize>(mut fields: [Field; N]) -> [Field; N] {
    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut index = 0;
    while index < N {
        fields[index].count = 1;
        let mut dimension = 0;
        while dimension < fields[index].shape.len() {
            fields[index].count *= fields[index].shape[dimension];
            dimension += 1;
        }
        fields[index].width = fields[index].dtype.width();
        fields[index].size = fields[index].count * fields[index].width;
        fields[index].offset = offset;
        offset += fields[index].size;
        index += 1;
    }
    fields
}
macro_rules! fields {
    ($($name:ident: $dtype:ident [$($dimension:literal),*]),* $(,)?) => {
        pub const FIELDS: &[Field] = &layout([$(Field {
            name: stringify!($name), shape: &[$($dimension),*], dtype: Dtype::$dtype,
            count: 0, width: 0, offset: 0, size: 0,
        }),*]);
    };
}
