frozen feature and action source. Adapters send complete history and decode
only newly appended engine events. Reset policies with the wall seed for each
game before starting a new cohort.

Drawn/held aliases, physical tile copies and exact policy ties use randomness
keyed by wall seed, acting seat, event count and decision phase. Candidate seat,
model identity, worker and batch position are excluded. This preserves fair
alias choices and common randomness across seat rotations. Evaluation manifests
record this contract; older unseeded matches require a fresh output directory.
Numerical model outputs can still change with inference batch shape, so full
replay equality across arbitrary batch sizes is not guaranteed.

Paired bootstrap summaries process resamples in bounded blocks while
preserving the seeded sampling sequence and reported confidence bounds.

```sh
python -m training.evaluate \
  --new /path/to/export/saved_model \
  --old /path/to/opponent/saved_model \
  --output /path/to/match \
  --games 10000 --seed 941 --workers 1 --devices GPU-UUID
```

| Rule | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| Each player loads its own frozen source | Reproduces its feature and model contract |
| Rotate each seed through four seats | Controls seat allocation |
| Use a game count divisible by four | Keeps complete seed groups |
| Repeat the unchanged command to resume | Reuses completed games |
| Keep both SavedModel contents unchanged | Resume validates every model file before reading results |
| Use disjoint seeds for each checkpoint | Later checkpoint matches do not reuse earlier training outcomes |

`evaluation.json` records SHA-256 hashes for every requested SavedModel file.
Changed models and manifests without these identities require a fresh output
directory, even when all games have completed.

`summary.json` reports placements, scores, ST3 points and paired uncertainty
bounds. Lower training loss alone does not establish stronger play.

TensorBoard events are written to `OUTPUT/tensorboard`, or to the directory
selected with `--tensorboard`. They report completed games, percent complete,
each side's metrics, and paired differences with confidence bounds. `new`
identifies the `--new` model; `old` identifies its opponents.

## Mortal opponent

The same harness accepts a Mortal checkpoint (`.pth` or a ZIP containing one
checkpoint) as the old opponent:

```sh
  --new /path/to/export/saved_model \

  --mortal-source /path/to/upstream-policy \
  --output /path/to/mortal-match \
  --games 4 --seed 941 --workers 1 --devices -1
```

Install PyTorch in the evaluator's Python environment. Use upstream Mortal
commit `0cff2b52982be5b1163aa9a62fb01f03ce91e0d2`, including its matching
`libriichi` extension. Build the extension with the same Python interpreter:

```sh
git -C /path/to/upstream-policy checkout 0cff2b52982be5b1163aa9a62fb01f03ce91e0d2
cd /path/to/upstream-policy
PYO3_PYTHON="$(command -v python)" cargo build --release --locked -p libriichi
python - <<'PY'

import shutil
import sysconfig

    "target/release/libriichi.so",
    pathlib.Path(sysconfig.get_paths()["platlib"]) / "libriichi.so",

```

The Linux adapter runs in a separate process, using only each seat's private
MJAI event stream. It follows
[Mortal's agent flow](https://riichi.dev/docs/mortal): call `react()` for every
event from `obs.new_events()`, then map the response with
`obs.select_action_from_mjai()`. A trailing delayed-dora announcement updates
Mortal's state without replacing the preceding decision response; successive
added kans can otherwise erase a valid rob-kan win. No action suppression or
automatic pass substitution is applied. It loads both state dictionaries
strictly, uses evaluation mode with greedy legal-action selection, and enables
upstream's win guard.
There is no training or exploration. RiichiEnv remains responsible for match
rules and rejects any action that cannot be mapped to a legal action.

Mortal matches use standard Tenhou south-game rules, with four-seat rotations
per seed. Our custom duplicate mode preserves per-seat draw queues, borrowing from
the backs of other queues counterclockwise when a queue empties. All seats
share the common rinshan replacements; exhaustion leaves 14 tiles globally.
Duplicate mode also changes match progression. Mortal matches use standard
rules and are recorded as `riichienv_standard_south`, separately from
`riichienv_duplicate_south`.

The match directory freezes the checkpoint, upstream model/engine source,
native extension, and adapter source. Their SHA-256 hashes are recorded in
`evaluation.json`; changing them requires a fresh output directory. The
extension is specific to its Python ABI and platform. Mortal's source and
weights remain external dependencies with their own licensing/provenance.

Start with a four-game smoke test. CPU inference is supported (`--devices -1`);
larger matches can use a training GPU UUID. Each worker shares one loaded
Mortal network across its opponent seats. Upstream bots process their event
streams independently; pending neural requests are combined into one engine
call and distributed back to their callers in order. `--batch-games` controls
the available parallel games. This preserves the upstream event flow and
float32 inference, though GPU batching can produce small rounding differences.
Measure full-game throughput and memory before increasing worker counts.

To exercise the integration test with a real checkpoint:

```sh
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 PYTHONPATH=. \
  python -m pytest integration/big/test_evaluation.py
```

`python -m training.checkpoint_match` exports a checkpoint and runs its

runner accepts this command as a JSON argument list; see

# Match records for critic fitting and MMD

## Build

Run conversion in a separate CPU process after the checkpoint match finishes:

```sh
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 python -m training.match_records \
  --matches /path/to/checkpoint-evaluation/matches \
  --output /path/to/new-critic-records --workers 16
```

The evaluator's `games.jsonl` and `evaluation.json` identify the complete
input set. The output directory must be new. Conversion writes compressed
TFRecord shards and `dataset.json` with exact game and position counts.
Keep generated records outside the source repository.

## Positions and targets

- Include every recoverable policy decision from all four seats, including
  Mortal's. Match MMD uses these as off-policy experience, not imitation labels.
- Do not apply AFK exclusions, focused sampling or training partitions.
- Share the recorded-action mapping with the expert replay reader.
- Keep censored call intentions excluded; an unrecorded losing claim is not
  evidence of a pass. Forced actions remain outside the decision contract.
- Supervise recorded current-hand payments, including accepted riichi
  deposits, with the same relative-seat contract as ordinary replay.
- Later game results are not a critic target.
- Leave unused hidden-hand, hindsight score, bonus and ron labels unknown.
  Conversion never reconstructs counterfactual scores from a winning hand.

These records use the existing numeric training-record schema. They do not
introduce a second feature encoding or a legacy format fallback.

## Consumer

`match_records.batches(output, batch_size, seed)` makes one finite shuffled
pass and retains the final partial batch. Each batch contains:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `features` | Decision-time model inputs |
| `chosen` | Canonical critic action ID |
| `head`, `legal` | Active policy head and legal action mask for MMD |
| `payment_points` | Observed relative-seat payment cells |

The trainer owns padding masks, optimizer state and the number of passes.
There are no imitation targets in this consumer. Match MMD uses detached
critic action values and KL penalties.

# Training objective

The active [match-then-root MMD loop](corrections/README.md) learns from complete
matches against Mortal, then balanced eligible/normal roots rerun in self-play.
All four seats contribute observed actions and current-hand outcomes. Root
selection changes the sampled states; forced choices and Mortal choices are
experience, not imitation labels. Every retained descendant trains the actor.

## Current-hand critic

```text
J = projected_settlement_ST3 / 100 + P(first) - P(fourth)
Q = sum(settlement_probability * J)
critic_loss = payment_nll + critic_constraint_loss
```

The critic fits observed payments for played actions. Unplayed alternatives
receive no settlement target. Each possible current-hand outcome is projected
through the fixed match-continuation mapping before taking expectations.
Terminal J uses rounded ST3/100 and the realized placement bonus; nonterminal
J uses calibrated single-Gumbel placement probabilities. Later realized match
outcomes are not targets. There is no state-value head or ST3 mean-loss term.
Padded rows contribute neither loss nor gradients.

[CriticTrainer](trainer.py) updates the shared encoder and critic from these
observed payments. Hidden-hand belief labels are not directly supervised in
this phase; shared beliefs receive indirect gradients through the critic.

## Magnetic mirror descent

```text
actor_loss = -sum((P(current) - P(previous)) * stop_gradient(Q))
           + 0.3 * KL(current || previous)
           + 0.3 * KL(current || fixed production)
           + 0.01 * structural_constraint_loss
```

The previous actor is frozen at each match/root phase boundary. The production
magnet stays fixed across the run. Both references and Q values are detached.
The previous-policy value term is a constant baseline. All legal actions enter
the objective; selected root pairs do not replace the legal distribution.
MMD uses gradient steps on this objective. There is no separate entropy bonus,
Q-weighted imitation, positive-action prior or downside-risk penalty.

Each phase fits the critic once and then trains the actor once. The shared
encoder can change in both stages. Actor updates do not fit critic weights
through Q, although their shared-feature changes can affect later forecasts.

| Supervision | Critic pass | MMD actor pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Observed payment likelihood and critic constraints | Yes | No |
| Detached expected legal-action Q | No | Yes |
| Previous and fixed-production KL | No | Yes |
| Actor structural constraints | No | Yes, weight 0.01 |
| Direct hidden-hand labels or imitation | No | No |

## Restoration and root eligibility

Supervised policy and belief losses and the [expert label decoder](restoration.py)
remain available for restoring prior structures. They do not run as improvement
stages. Sakigiri witnesses select eligible roots only; the policy has neither
a dedicated sakigiri scalar nor a separate sakigiri loss.

Calls must strictly reduce shanten to qualify as targeted roots; a pass is
eligible when an improving call exists. Disagreement roots compare policy
choice against max-Q with a 0.0025 objective gap. Normal roots balance targeted
roots. Native legality and normal trajectories retain all legal choices.

Forecasts condition on attempting a call, including attempts preempted by other
players. Accepted-call features describe a hypothetical candidate, while hard
scoring constraints use guaranteed pre-call facts. Planned discards are
contingent on acceptance.

## Validation and ownership

[Settlement support](../model/joint_settlement.py) owns hard outcome rules;
[critic statistics](../model/critic.py) own streaming likelihood and Q;
[model constraints](../model/CONSTRAINTS.md) own detached structural targets;
[MMD training](corrections/trainer.py) owns actor losses.

Check settlement likelihood, legal-policy entropy, both KLs, gradient norms
and independent match results. Raw ST3 reporting stays in its original units;
J includes placement bonuses and cannot be converted back by multiplying by
100. Non-finite gradients fail before updates. Lower training losses alone do
not establish stronger play.

# Training

The active loop is [match-then-root magnetic mirror descent](corrections/README.md).
Play 10,000 matches against Mortal, train on all four seats, select a balanced
mixture of eligible and normal roots, and train again on self-play reruns.
Both phases update the actor at every retained decision, including descendants.

Expert imitation is reserved for restoring learned structures. The
[restoration labels](restoration.py), the finite
[dataset reader](../log_dataset/training_data.py), dataset preparation and model supervised
losses remain available; they are not improvement stages in the MMD loop.

import argparse
import hashlib

import subprocess
import sys


def run(args):
    if args.games <= 0 or args.games % 4:
        raise ValueError("Evaluation needs complete four-game seed groups")
    root = pathlib.Path(args.output)
    if (root / "policy").exists():
        verification = json.loads(
            (root / "policy" / "export-verification.json").read_text()
        )
        if (
            verification["weight_sha256"]
            != hashlib.sha256(
                pathlib.Path(args.weights).read_bytes()
            ).hexdigest()
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "Existing evaluation export uses different weights"
            )
    else:
        subprocess.run(
            [
                sys.executable,
                "-m",
                "model.export",
                "--weights",
                args.weights,
                "--self-play-seed",
                "941",
                "--output",
                str(root / "policy"),
            ],
            check=True,
        )
    subprocess.run(
        [
            sys.executable,
            "-m",
            "training.evaluate",
            "--new",
            str(root / "policy" / "saved_model"),
            "--old",
            args.opponent,
            "--output",
            str(root / "matches"),
            "--games",
            str(args.games),
            "--seed",
            str(args.seed),
            "--workers",
            str(args.workers),
            "--devices",
            args.devices,
            "--batch-games",
            str(args.batch_games),
            *(
                ["--mortal-source", args.mortal_source]
                if args.mortal_source
                else []
            ),
        ],
        check=True,
    )


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    for name in ("weights", "opponent", "output"):
        parser.add_argument("--" + name, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--mortal-source")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, required=True)

    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-games", type=int, default=8)
    parser.add_argument("--devices", default="-1")
    run(parser.parse_args())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Match and root magnetic mirror descent

## Source layout

Read [run.py](run.py) for the complete training sequence. The package separates
that sequence from root selection, artifact storage and replica coordination.

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| [__main__.py](__main__.py) | Command-line arguments and failure reporting |
| [run.py](run.py) | Launch validation, checkpoints and match/root training stages |
| [matches.py](matches.py) | Validate match manifests and replay recorded decisions |
| [collection.py](collection.py) | Select balanced roots and simulate their continuations |
| [rollouts.py](rollouts.py) | Collect a round in chunks, write receipts and read packed shards |
| [trainer.py](trainer.py) | MMD actor objective and updates |
| [distributed.py](distributed.py) | Replica updates, stop coordination and stage publication |

The shared [critic trainer](../trainer.py), [match records](../match_records.py)
and [self-play engine](../self_play.py) live one level up. Collection returns
decision batches; rollout storage owns filenames and serialization. The runner
coordinates stages and keeps the optimizers alive across rounds.

## Training sequence

The loop is:

1. Play 10,000 standard South games against the fixed Mortal opponent, using
   2,500 wall seeds with four learner-seat rotations each.
2. Fit the critic on all recoverable decisions from **all four seats**, including
   Mortal's, then run one MMD actor pass over those positions. Observed actions
   and settlements supervise the critic; the actor uses estimated action values,
   not cross-entropy targets copying Mortal's choices.
3. Select targeted starts from the match logs and balance them with an equal
   number of uniformly sampled ordinary starts. Rerun these starts in
   **self-play**, using the policy after match training.
4. Fit the critic on every decision in those reruns, then run one MMD actor pass
   over the same decisions, including forced roots and all descendants.
5. Evaluate the resulting checkpoint in a fresh 10,000-game Mortal match. That
   match supplies the next iteration; the last match is not subsequently trained.

Imitation is reserved for
restoring prior structures in a separate restoration step; it is not part of the
MMD improvement loop. There is no outcome-winning filter, separate sakigiri loss,
or entropy bonus.

Mortal trajectories are off-policy experience: their settlements reflect Mortal's
subsequent play and the original seat-specific opponents. They are not unbiased
estimates of our policy's returns. Self-play reruns provide new outcome evidence
under our policy. The same MMD objective applies to positions from either source.

## Shared learning rule

Both actor phases minimize the same neural MMD objective:

```text
-E_pi[stop_gradient(Q)]
+ 0.3 KL(pi || previous_policy)
+ 0.3 KL(pi || fixed_production)
+ 0.01 constraint_loss
```

Subtracting the previous policy's expected Q provides a constant baseline.
Q uses `J = ST3/100 + P(first) - P(fourth)`, with scale 1 in this runner.
The previous policy refreshes at the start of each match/root learning phase,
then remains frozen through critic fitting and actor updates. The production
magnet never refreshes. Actor loss does not backpropagate through Q or update
critic-owned weights.
The critic and actor have separate AdamW optimizers, both at learning rate 5e-6.

This is a gradient-based neural approximation to the statewise
[magnetic mirror descent objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.05825), not an
exact tabular solve or a four-player equilibrium guarantee. The actor evaluates
all legal actions using the learned critic; forcing a root action does not turn
that action into an imitation target. Win/pass still shares the model's one
current-hand forecast and therefore gets no value-based accept/decline gradient.

Critic supervision remains observed **current-hand settlements**, with shared
encoder gradients and the existing payment likelihood and structural constraints.
The fixed continuation mapping projects those settlements to J. Match training
covers all four seats throughout each game; it does not introduce final-game return
regression or a state-value head. Root reruns currently stop at hand settlement.
Root archives retain payment cells; unused twelve-value continuation-state
metadata is no longer serialized. Generate fresh archives for the current
contract without rewriting retained historical artifacts.
The critic fits each phase before its actor pass, so new outcomes can affect
policy improvement even when a pair has identical realized settlements.

## Root selection

Positions from all four seats in the Mortal match are eligible starts. One
category is assigned per game before scanning it:

| Category | Eligibility / exploration |
| --- | --- |
| Q disagreement | Policy discard versus max-Q discard, gap at least 0.0025 J |
| Tenpai | Opposite sides of the keep/break-shanten boundary |
| Keiten | Same structural comparison within one shanten and at most 16 live tiles |
| Calls | Strictly improving call/kan versus declining |
| Riichi | Declaration versus dama, preferring the same discard |
| Threat | Different genbutsu safety against riichi or two-open-meld seats |
| Sakigiri | Verified completion-preserving discard-order witnesses from the logged hand |

Each non-Q category uses a uniform reservoir over eligible decisions. Q
sampling keeps up to eight proposals, then selects a qualifying disagreement.
Sakigiri reuses the existing witness miner; its hindsight ron evidence selects
starts only. Its preferred/other ordering and weights never supervise the actor.
Both legal witness actions are rerun, and their new outcomes train the critic.
Sakigiri is a root-selection criterion only. The policy has no learned
`sakigiri_order` scalar or dedicated sakigiri loss.

Every selected target is accompanied by one uniform normal root from the same
source game. Normal means unfiltered, so it can also meet a targeted criterion.
The balance is **50/50 root starts**, not equal descendant counts. Both groups
receive two continuations. Targeted branches force the two proposed actions on
a shared unseen wall. Normal branches sample their first actions from the frozen
policy and use independent wall seeds. Subsequent actions sample the frozen
policy in all four seats. Opponent hands remain fixed within each fork; this is
not posterior resampling of hidden hands.

All decisions from every continuation train once per phase. Rollout files are
batched separately, and each update averages its valid rows; partial batches
therefore affect per-row step weighting. Longer trajectories provide more rows.
Mortal is used for match generation only; roots use frozen self-play.
No root selection depends on the new continuation outcomes.

## Run

The evaluator command must contain `--games 10000`, `--seed`, `--mortal-source`,
and `{weights}` / `{output}` placeholders. Save an argument list such as this
as `evaluation-command.json`:

```json
["python", "-m", "training.checkpoint_match",
 "--weights", "{weights}", "--output", "{output}",
 "--opponent", "/path/to/mortal-checkpoint.zip",
 "--mortal-source", "/path/to/Mortal",
 "--games", "10000", "--seed", "2100000000",
 "--workers", "2", "--devices", "GPU-TRAIN-A,GPU-TRAIN-B"]
```

```sh
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=GPU-LEARNER python -m training.corrections \
  --initial /path/to/initial.weights.h5 \
  --reference /path/to/fixed-production/saved_model \
  --output /path/to/new-run/candidate \
  --evaluation-command evaluation-command.json \
  --rounds 5 --root-games 10000 --batch-size 64 --workers 16 --seed 941
```

Each match advances its base seed by 2,500. `--root-games` is the number of games
sampled without replacement from the current match for root mining, not a
promise that every game yields a target. Match MMD always uses all 10,000 games.
Every invocation starts new optimizers, counters and output files; prior runs
are not resumed. Existing stopped-run files retain their historical meanings.

## Multiple learner workers

Set `TF_CONFIG` with the same worker list in every process and a distinct
worker index. Select one GPU per process with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`. Worker 0
owns evaluation, conversion, root mining, checkpoints and progress files.
Other workers wait on CPU while those stages run. All workers create the model
and both optimizers once; optimizer state persists through every phase and
round. The mirror refreshes on every worker at each learning phase.

`--batch-size` is the global valid-row budget. Each replica receives a physical
batch of `ceil(batch_size / replicas)` rows, repeating the final input row for
padding. Valid counts exclude padding, including entirely padded replicas.
Masked statistics are normalized globally; both losses divide by replica count
for differentiation. Dense gradients are summed before per-variable clipping
at norm 1, followed by one AdamW update. The optimizer performs no second sum.
The reported norm is `gradient/global_norm`; `plan.json` records `replicas`.

When workers use separate filesystems, provide `--sync-command` pointing to a
JSON argument list with `{root}` and `{stage}` placeholders. The chief writes
`{stage}-ready.pending.json`, then runs that command. The command must copy the
stage's generated inputs and publish the pending JSON on the remote host as
`{stage}-ready.json` **after** all inputs arrive. On return, the chief renames
its own pending file to the ready file. Workers then enter a short barrier.

| Stage | Generated inputs to synchronize |
| --- | --- |
| `round-N-match` | `round-N-match-data/` |
| `round-N-roots` | `round-N-*-rollouts.npz` and `round-N-rollouts.json` |
| `complete` | Ready marker only |

A marker with `stopped: true` needs no input transfer. Checkpoint and match
provenance remain on the chief. Dataset shards and rollout filenames are
relative to each host's output root, so the two roots need not match. Workers
remain alive through the final evaluation and exit after the complete marker.
The launcher must stop all peers if a worker fails.

Artifacts include initial and phase checkpoints, completed match replays,
all-seat TFRecords, root selection receipts, and compressed rollout shards.
Rollouts use the existing lossless `PackedBatch` encoding with canonical critic
action IDs. Every shard is consumed including its final partial batch. Only
one shard is loaded at a time. Counters distinguish actor and critic exposures.
Rollout manifests list only games in completed mining chunks, including when
`STOP` interrupts a round.
Put run artifacts on the configured artifact volume, outside the repository.

Create `STOP` to stop after the current match, conversion, collection chunk or
update batch. Completed artifacts and the latest trained weights are preserved.
Match results describe the checkpoint **before** learning from that match;
post-match checkpoints require the next fresh match for strength evidence.

import json
import os
import pathlib
import sys
import time

from training import monitor


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    for name in ("initial", "reference", "output", "evaluation-command"):
        parser.add_argument("--" + name, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=5)
    parser.add_argument("--root-games", type=int, default=10000)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=64)
    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=16)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--sync-command")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    from training.corrections import run

    existing_output = pathlib.Path(args.output).exists()
    try:
        run.run(args)
    finally:
        path = pathlib.Path(args.output) / "status.json"
        if (
            (
                "TF_CONFIG" not in os.environ
                or json.loads(os.environ["TF_CONFIG"])["task"]["index"] == 0
            )
            and not existing_output
            and sys.exception() is not None
            and path.exists()
        ):
            status = json.loads(path.read_text())
            status.update(
                stage="failed",
                error=str(sys.exception()),
                updated_at=time.time(),
            )
            monitor.write_json(path, status)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Mortal matches, match MMD, then MMD on balanced targeted-root reruns."""

import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import numpy
import tensorflow as tf

from model import export
from training import match_records, monitor, self_play
from training import trainer as base_trainer
from training.corrections import (
    collection,
    distributed,
    matches,
    rollouts,
    trainer,
)


def evaluate(command, weights, output, round_number):
    command = command.copy()
    seed_argument = command.index("--seed") + 1
    games = int(command[command.index("--games") + 1])
    command[seed_argument] = str(
        int(command[seed_argument]) + round_number * (games // 4)
    )
    subprocess.run(
        [
            value.format(weights=str(weights), output=str(output))
            for value in command
        ],
        check=True,
    )


def validate_launch(args):
    if min(args.rounds, args.root_games, args.batch_size, args.workers) <= 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "Round, root-game, batch and worker budgets must be positive"
        )
    if args.root_games > 10000:
        raise ValueError("Root games cannot exceed the 10,000-game match")
    command = json.loads(pathlib.Path(args.evaluation_command).read_text())
    if int(command[command.index("--games") + 1]) != 10000:
        raise ValueError("Each Mortal match must contain 10,000 games")
    if "--mortal-source" not in command:
        raise ValueError("The match command must select a Mortal source")
    int(command[command.index("--seed") + 1])
    if not all(
        any(placeholder in value for value in command)
        for placeholder in ("{weights}", "{output}")
    ):
        raise ValueError("Evaluation command needs {weights} and {output}")
    if args.sync_command:
        sync = json.loads(pathlib.Path(args.sync_command).read_text())
        if not all(
            any(placeholder in value for value in sync)
            for placeholder in ("{root}", "{stage}")
        ):
            raise ValueError("Sync command needs {root} and {stage}")
    devices = tf.config.list_physical_devices("GPU")
    if len(devices) > 1:
        raise ValueError("Select one learner GPU by UUID")
    for device in devices:
        tf.config.experimental.set_memory_growth(device, True)
    tf.keras.utils.set_random_seed(args.seed)
    return command


def save_checkpoint(network, root, name):
    weights = root / f"{name}.weights.h5"
    network.save_weights(weights)
    pending = root / "latest.weights.h5.pending"
    pending.symlink_to(weights.name)
    pending.replace(root / "latest.weights.h5")
    return weights


def train_phase(*, phase, batches, learner, root, progress, report, group):
    """Fit all observed outcomes, then actor rows, with persistent optimizers."""
    learner.mirror.set_weights(learner.network.actor.get_weights())
    for update in ("critic", "actor"):
        for batch in batches():
            if group.stopped(root):
                return
            metrics = group.update(update, batch)
            progress[update + "_exposures"] += len(batch["chosen"])
            if group.chief:
                report(
                    phase + "-" + update,
                    {name: float(value) for name, value in metrics.items()},
                )


def run(args):
    command = validate_launch(args)
    group = distributed.LearnerGroup()
    root = pathlib.Path(args.output).resolve()
    if group.chief:
        root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    with group.strategy.scope():
        features = self_play.initial_features(args.seed)
        network = export.load_network(args.initial, features)
        previous = export.load_network(args.initial, features).actor
        previous.trainable = False
        magnet = tf.saved_model.load(args.reference)
        learner = trainer.MMDTrainer(
            network=network,
            mirror=previous,
            magnet=magnet.signatures["policy"],
            learning_rate=5e-6,
        )
        critic_learner = base_trainer.CriticTrainer(network, features, 5e-6)
    group.bind(learner, critic_learner, args.batch_size)
    if group.chief:
        weights = save_checkpoint(network, root, "initial")
        monitor.write_json(
            root / "plan.json",
            {
                **vars(args),
                "method": "match-then-root-magnetic-mirror-descent",
                "replicas": group.replicas,
                "evaluation_argv": command,
                "learning_rate": 5e-6,
                "mirror_coefficient": 0.3,
                "magnet_coefficient": 0.3,
                "objective_scale": 1.0,
                "match_training_seats": [0, 1, 2, 3],
                "root_selection_seats": [0, 1, 2, 3],
                "targeted_root_fraction": 0.5,
                "continuations_per_root": 2,
                "continuation_policy": "sampled-frozen-self-play",
                "continuation_horizon": "current-hand",
                "critic_passes_per_phase": 1,
                "actor_passes_per_phase": 1,
                "initial_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
                    pathlib.Path(args.initial).read_bytes()
                ).hexdigest(),
                "reference_files_sha256": {
                    str(path.relative_to(args.reference)): hashlib.sha256(
                        path.read_bytes()
                    ).hexdigest()
                    for path in sorted(pathlib.Path(args.reference).rglob("*"))
                    if path.is_file()
                },
            },
        )
    packed_predict = self_play.predictor(network.actor)

    def predict(rows):
        return packed_predict({name: rows[name] for name in rows.dtype.names})

    root_evaluate = collection.root_scorer(network)
    writer = (
        tf.summary.create_file_writer(str(root / "tensorboard"))
        if group.chief
        else None
    )
    generator = numpy.random.default_rng(args.seed)
    progress = {"actor_exposures": 0, "critic_exposures": 0}
    started = time.monotonic()
    round_number = 0

    def report(stage, metrics):
        status = {
            "stage": stage,
            "round": round_number,
            "phase_name": f"round-{round_number}",
            "rounds": args.rounds,
            "exposures": progress["actor_exposures"],
            **progress,
            "elapsed_seconds": time.monotonic() - started,
            "updated_at": time.time(),
            **metrics,
        }
        monitor.write_json(root / "status.json", status)
        with (root / "progress.jsonl").open("a") as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps(status) + "\n")
        with writer.as_default():
            for name, value in metrics.items():
                tf.summary.scalar(
                    stage + "/" + name,
                    value,
                    step=sum(progress.values()),
                )
        writer.flush()

    if group.chief:
        report("evaluation", {})
        evaluate(command, weights, root / "initial-evaluation", 0)
    match_directory = root / "initial-evaluation" / "matches"
    for round_number in range(1, args.rounds + 1):
        data = root / f"round-{round_number}-match-data"
        if group.chief and not (root / "STOP").exists():
            recorded = matches.sources(match_directory)
            report("match-records", {})
            subprocess.run(
                [
                    sys.executable,
                    "-m",
                    "training.match_records",
                    "--matches",
                    str(match_directory),
                    "--output",
                    str(data),
                    "--workers",
                    str(args.workers),
                ],
                check=True,
            )
        if distributed.publish_stage(
            args, group, root, f"round-{round_number}-match"
        ):
            break
        train_phase(
            phase="match",
            learner=learner,
            root=root,
            progress=progress,
            report=report,
            group=group,
            batches=lambda: match_records.batches(
                data, args.batch_size, args.seed + round_number
            ),
        )
        if group.chief:
            weights = save_checkpoint(
                network, root, f"round-{round_number}-match"
            )
        if group.chief and not (root / "STOP").exists():
            rollouts.collect(
                root=root,
                round_number=round_number,
                match_directory=match_directory,
                recorded=recorded,
                order=generator.permutation(len(recorded))[: args.root_games],
                seed=args.seed + round_number * 100000,
                predict=predict,
                root_evaluate=root_evaluate,
                packing=critic_learner.feature_packing,
                report=report,
            )
        if distributed.publish_stage(
            args, group, root, f"round-{round_number}-roots"
        ):
            break
        manifest = json.loads(
            (root / f"round-{round_number}-rollouts.json").read_text()
        )
        rollout_files = [root / name for name in manifest["files"]]
        if not rollout_files:
            raise ValueError("Match pool yielded no eligible targeted roots")
        train_phase(
            phase="roots",
            learner=learner,
            root=root,
            progress=progress,
            report=report,
            group=group,
            batches=lambda: rollouts.batches(
                rollout_files,
                critic_learner.feature_packing,
                args.batch_size,
                args.seed + round_number,
            ),
        )
        if group.chief:
            weights = save_checkpoint(network, root, f"round-{round_number}")
            if not (root / "STOP").exists():
                report("evaluation", {})
                evaluate(
                    command,
                    weights,
                    root / f"round-{round_number}-evaluation",
                    round_number,
                )
                report("round-complete", {})
        match_directory = root / f"round-{round_number}-evaluation" / "matches"
    if group.chief:
        report("stopped" if (root / "STOP").exists() else "complete", {})
        writer.close()
    distributed.publish_stage(args, group, root, "complete")

"""Current-hand critic records from completed evaluation match logs."""

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import gzip
import json
import multiprocessing
import pathlib

import numpy
import tensorflow as tf

from log_dataset import features, records, replay, scoring, training_data
from model import critic, outcomes
from training import restoration


def game_records(path):
    """All recoverable choices, without hindsight rescoring or AFK filtering."""
    path = pathlib.Path(path)
    with gzip.open(path, "rt") as stream:
        events = [json.loads(line) for line in stream]
    outcomes.normalize_draw_payments(events)
    starts = [
        index
        for index, event in enumerate(events)
        if event["type"] == "start_kyoku"
    ]
    for start, end in zip(starts, starts[1:] + [len(events)]):
        state = replay.Replay(path.stem, events[start:end])
        payments = outcomes.terminal_payments(events[start:end])
        target = {
            "payment": payments,
            "bonus": numpy.full((4, 4, 4), -1, numpy.int16),
            "score": numpy.full(
                (4, 4, 4, len(scoring.BONUS_HAN)), -1, numpy.int16
            ),
        }
        for (
            index,
            actor,
            phase,
            next_index,
            win_choices,
        ) in state.policy_decisions():
            observation = replay.Observation(
                game_id=path.stem,
                kyoku_id=state.kyoku_id,
                decision_index=state.decision_index,
                actor=actor,
                features=features.pack(state, actor, phase),
            )
            for name, definition in records.LABELS.items():
                setattr(
                    observation,
                    name,
                    numpy.full(definition["shape"], -1, definition["dtype"]),
                )
            observation.terminal_payment = outcomes.relative_payments(
                payments, actor, state.accepted
            )
            state.recorded_action(
                observation=observation,
                phase=phase,
                next_index=next_index,
                win_choices=win_choices,
            )
            yield training_data.serialize(observation, target)


def write_shard(task):
    tf.config.set_visible_devices([], "GPU")
    path, games = task
    positions = 0
    with tf.io.TFRecordWriter(str(path) + ".partial", options="GZIP") as writer:
        for game in games:
            for raw in game_records(game):
                writer.write(raw)
                positions += 1
    pathlib.Path(str(path) + ".partial").replace(path)
    return {"path": path.name, "games": len(games), "positions": positions}


def decode_records(raw):
    """Chosen critic action and observed payments, with no actor targets."""
    features, labels = records.parse_batch(raw)
    head, _, legal = restoration.policy_choices(features, labels)
    return {
        "head": head,
        "legal": legal,
        "features": features,
        "chosen": critic.chosen_actions(features, labels),
        "payment_points": tf.gather(
            tf.reshape(labels["terminal_payment"], [-1, 64]),
            numpy.ravel_multi_index(numpy.asarray(scoring.CELLS).T, (4, 4, 4)),
            axis=1,
        ),
    }


def batches(output, batch_size, seed):
    """One finite shuffled pass, including every row in the final batch."""
    output = pathlib.Path(output)
    manifest = json.loads((output / "dataset.json").read_text())
    return (
        tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices(
            [str(output / row["path"]) for row in manifest["shards"]]
        )
        .shuffle(len(manifest["shards"]), seed=seed)
        .interleave(
            lambda path: tf.data.TFRecordDataset(path, compression_type="GZIP"),
            cycle_length=8,
            block_length=64,
            num_parallel_calls=4,
            deterministic=True,
        )
        .shuffle(8192, seed=seed)
        .batch(batch_size)
        .map(decode_records, num_parallel_calls=2)
        .prefetch(2)
    )


def build(matches, output, workers):
    """Convert the completed evaluator manifest in isolated CPU workers."""
    matches = pathlib.Path(matches)
    output = pathlib.Path(output)
    manifest = json.loads((matches / "evaluation.json").read_text())
    games = [
        json.loads(line)
        for line in (matches / "games.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()
    ]
    assert len(games) == manifest["games"]
    paths = sorted(matches / game["replay"] for game in games)
    assert len(set(paths)) == len(paths)
    output.mkdir(parents=True)
    with concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor(
        max_workers=workers,
        mp_context=multiprocessing.get_context("spawn"),
    ) as pool:
        shards = list(
            pool.map(
                write_shard,
                [
                    (
                        output / f"train-{start // 100:04d}.tfrecord.gz",
                        paths[start : start + 100],
                    )
                    for start in range(0, len(paths), 100)
                ],
            )
        )
    result = {
        "games": len(games),
        "positions": sum(row["positions"] for row in shards),
        "shards": shards,
    }
    (output / "dataset.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    return result


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--matches", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=16)
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    print(
        json.dumps(
            build(
                arguments.matches,
                arguments.output,
                arguments.workers,
            )
        )
    )

"""Atomic progress metadata for training and monitoring."""

import json


def write_json(path, value):
    """Replace run metadata atomically so readers never see partial JSON."""
    temporary = path.with_suffix(".partial")
    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2) + "\n")
    temporary.replace(path)

"""Expert records and policy labels for structural restoration."""

import tensorflow as tf

from model import actions


def policy_choices(features, labels):
    """Recover the active policy head, observed choice and legal mask."""
    choices = tf.stack(
        [
            tf.cast(labels[name], tf.int32)
            for name in actions.TRAIN_POLICY_HEADS
        ],
        axis=1,
    )
    tf.debugging.assert_equal(
        tf.reduce_sum(tf.cast(choices >= 0, tf.int32), axis=1), 1
    )
    head = tf.argmax(choices >= 0, axis=1, output_type=tf.int32)
    expert = tf.gather(choices, head, batch_dims=1)
    masks = actions.legal_choices(features)
    legal = tf.gather(
        tf.stack(
            [
                tf.pad(masks[name], [[0, 0], [0, 150 - masks[name].shape[-1]]])
                for name in actions.TRAIN_POLICY_HEADS
            ],
            axis=1,
        ),
        head,
        batch_dims=1,
    )
    tf.debugging.assert_equal(tf.gather(legal, expert, batch_dims=1), True)
    return head, expert, legal
